newsitem.title: UK: Motor racing-Grand Prix business not racing to stock offering.
newsitem.headline: Motor racing-Grand Prix business not racing to stock offering.

text.p: The prospect of investors buying shares in Formula One motor racing stalled Sunday when the sport's top businessman told a British newspaper he had no wish to hurry toward a stock offering.
"My feeling is to wait and see" about offering shares to other investors, Bernie Ecclestone said, according to an interview published in the Sunday Times.
He also said that in any event he would want to retain a majority stake in the sport he presently controls.
He said Salomon Bros., the investment bank he has hired to advise him, had told him his attitude was silly.
"They may have wanted to put pressure on me. One thing is for sure -- it certainly won't force me to do it," Ecclestone said.

The entrepreneur, president of a major Formula One association and owner of the sport's promotion arm, has transformed Grand Prix racing into a big business that attracts 450 million television viewers for major events.

Already a multimillionaire and one of the richest men in Britain, where he lives in a mansion in the Chelsea section of London, he stands to make about 2 billion pounds ($3.2 billion) if a stock offering proceeds, according to investment bankers.
He said he may wait until money starts to flow in from deals with pay television channels. These, he said, could "bring in an enormous profit and give Formula One its full worth."
If a stock offer goes ahead, it could capitalise on British investors' thirst for high-profile sports businesses.
Newcastle United is currently one of several top soccer clubs planning to join Manchester United and Tottenham Hotspur by listing its shares on the stock market.
